html:
The Eritrean Ascari were African soldiers of the Royal Corps of Eritrean Colonial Troops, the army Italy raised in Eritrea from the 1880s until 1941.

Service paid well, and by the 1930s a large share of Eritrean men of fighting age had served. They fought for Italy in Libya and Somalia, and formed a core of the army in the invasion of Ethiopia in 1935.

They fought hard against the British in 1941, notably at Keren. Their shared service gave many Eritreans a sense of standing apart from Ethiopia, which fed later demands for independence. Veterans are remembered in Asmara, capital of Italian Eritrea.
sum: The Eritrean Ascari were African soldiers of the Royal Corps of Eritrean Colonial Troops, the army Italy raised in Eritrea from the 1880s until 1941.
